mandarinMeaning: everyone; everybody (also: a great master in a field)
vietnameseMeaning: a tycoon; a rich and powerful person
note: One of the highest-frequency words in Mandarin and a total mismatch. 大家好 is 'hello everyone', not 'hello tycoon'. Mandarin does keep a rarer 'great expert' sense, which is where the Vietnamese meaning branched from.

mandarinMeaning: difficulty; hardship; difficult
vietnameseMeaning: despicable, contemptible, scummy (a strong insult)
note: In Vietnamese this is an insult aimed at a person's character. Saying it where Mandarin means 'this is difficult' is a serious misfire. Vietnamese uses khó khăn for the Mandarin sense.

mandarinMeaning: convenient; to facilitate (also a euphemism for using the toilet)
vietnameseMeaning: a vehicle; a means, medium or instrument
note: Mandarin uses it as an adjective/verb, Vietnamese as a concrete noun. phương tiện giao thông is 'means of transport', while 交通方便 means 'transport is convenient'.

mandarinMeaning: a PhD; a doctorate holder
vietnameseMeaning: a medical doctor; a physician
note: Both mean 'doctor' but of different kinds. A Mandarin 博士 is an academic; a Vietnamese bác sĩ treats patients. Mandarin for the medical sense is 医生 yīshēng, and Vietnamese for the academic one is tiến sĩ (from 进士).

mandarinMeaning: facial expression; to express one's feelings
vietnameseMeaning: a public demonstration; a protest
note: Both come from 'express + feeling' but landed in completely different places — a face versus a crowd in the street.

mandarinMeaning: a light snack; pastry; dim sum
vietnameseMeaning: breakfast
note: Vietnamese narrowed it to the morning meal specifically; Mandarin means a snack at any hour. Close enough to be tempting, wrong often enough to matter.

mandarinMeaning: to harm; to injure; to hurt
vietnameseMeaning: to pity; to feel sorry for
note: Near opposites in effect: Mandarin is the agent doing damage, Vietnamese is sympathy for the damaged. Vietnamese reanalysed thương as the native word for 'love/compassion'.

mandarinMeaning: to use; to utilize; to make use of (neutral)
vietnameseMeaning: to exploit; to take advantage of someone (pejorative)
note: Mandarin 利用资源 'utilize resources' is perfectly neutral. Vietnamese lợi dụng always implies unfair advantage taken of a person.

mandarinMeaning: as you like; casual; informal; whatever you prefer
vietnameseMeaning: careless, arbitrary, done without proper regard for rules
note: Mandarin 随便 is an easygoing invitation ('whatever you like'). Vietnamese tùy tiện is a criticism. Mandarin does have a secondary negative 'negligent' sense, which is the overlap that makes this confusing.

mandarinMeaning: hygiene; sanitation; hygienic
vietnameseMeaning: hygiene, but in everyday speech chiefly 'toilet' / 'to relieve oneself'
note: The literal senses agree; usage does not. Vietnamese đi vệ sinh is 'go to the toilet', and nhà vệ sinh is the toilet itself. Mandarin uses 卫生间 for the room.

mandarinMeaning: oneself; one's own
vietnameseMeaning: autistic; withdrawn, self-absorbed (colloquially)
note: 极 high-frequency in Mandarin as an ordinary reflexive pronoun. Vietnamese tự kỷ is a clinical/colloquial term about a person's psychology and never a pronoun.

mandarinMeaning: to be careful; watch out; take care
vietnameseMeaning: narrow-minded; petty; mean-spirited
note: A Mandarin sign reading 小心 is warning you to be careful, not calling anyone petty.

mandarinMeaning: comrade (political address); (slang) a gay person
vietnameseMeaning: comrade (political address only)
note: The political sense is shared, but Mandarin has a widespread slang sense that Vietnamese lacks entirely, so the word carries connotations in China a Vietnamese speaker will not expect.

mandarinMeaning: to sympathize with; sympathy; compassion
vietnameseMeaning: to agree; to concur; to be in accord
note: Mandarin is about feeling for someone's plight; Vietnamese is about agreeing with a position. Vietnamese for the Mandarin sense is thông cảm.

mandarinMeaning: husband
vietnameseMeaning: a heroic, manly man (literary, not a marital relation)
note: Mandarin is a plain kinship term. Vietnamese trượng phu is elevated and literary, never how you refer to your spouse (that is chồng).

mandarinMeaning: wife (colloquial, affectionate)
vietnameseMeaning: an old woman (plain descriptive, not affectionate)
note: Mandarin 老婆 is warm and marital. Vietnamese lão bà just means an elderly woman and would be odd or rude aimed at a spouse.

mandarinMeaning: teacher (the standard, respectful everyday word)
vietnameseMeaning: an old master (archaic/wuxia flavour)
note: 老师 is the ordinary word you call any teacher in China. Vietnamese uses giáo viên or thầy/cô; lão sư sounds like a martial-arts novel.

mandarinMeaning: teacher; schoolteacher (any level)
vietnameseMeaning: professor (the highest academic rank)
note: A significant status gap. Calling a Chinese primary-school 教师 a giáo sư in Vietnamese promotes them several ranks. Mandarin for professor is 教授 jiàoshòu.

mandarinMeaning: primary school (the institution)
vietnameseMeaning: primary education (the stage of study)
note: Mild but real: Mandarin names a building you attend, Vietnamese names a level of schooling. Vietnamese says trường tiểu học for the institution.

mandarinMeaning: a student at any level, including university
vietnameseMeaning: a school pupil, K-12 only
note: A university student in Vietnamese is sinh viên, never học sinh. In Mandarin 大学生 is still a 学生. Easy to get subtly wrong.

mandarinMeaning: nervous; tense; anxious; (of supply) tight, scarce
vietnameseMeaning: urgent; pressing; to hurry up
note: Mandarin describes an emotional state; Vietnamese describes time pressure. 我很紧张 is 'I'm nervous', not 'I'm in a hurry'.

mandarinMeaning: an old-style inn or guest house (dated/rustic)
vietnameseMeaning: a hotel (the ordinary modern word)
note: Vietnamese khách sạn is where you book a modern hotel room. Mandarin 客栈 evokes a historical roadside inn; the modern word is 酒店 or 宾馆.

mandarinMeaning: maybe; possibly; possible; probability
vietnameseMeaning: ability, capability (a person's competence); also possibility
note: The dominant Vietnamese sense is a person's skill — khả năng tiếng Anh 'English ability'. Mandarin 可能 never means competence; that is 能力 nénglì.

mandarinMeaning: quality (of goods or services), as well as of a person
vietnameseMeaning: moral character, virtue (of a person)
note: Vietnamese phẩm chất is chiefly about moral fibre. For product quality Vietnamese says chất lượng, while Mandarin 品质 covers both.

mandarinMeaning: a place; a spot; somewhere (everyday, concrete)
vietnameseMeaning: local; regional (as opposed to central government)
note: Mandarin's ordinary sense is 'place' — 这个地方 'this place'. Vietnamese địa phương is an administrative adjective. Mandarin does have that second sense (dìfāng, different tone) but it is not the common one.

mandarinMeaning: work; job; to work (the general everyday word)
vietnameseMeaning: an official assignment or mission; a work trip
note: Vietnamese đi công tác is 'go on a business trip'. The general Vietnamese word for work is công việc or làm việc. Mandarin 工作 is the neutral catch-all.

mandarinMeaning: engineering; an engineering project
vietnameseMeaning: a construction work; a completed structure or public works
note: Mandarin covers the discipline of engineering (软件工程 'software engineering'); Vietnamese công trình points at a physical built thing. Vietnamese for the discipline is kỹ thuật/công nghệ.

mandarinMeaning: a cadre; a leading official or manager
vietnameseMeaning: any state employee or party worker, right down to junior staff
note: Mandarin implies rank and leadership; Vietnamese cán bộ is far broader and covers ordinary civil servants.

mandarinMeaning: an article; an essay; a piece of writing
vietnameseMeaning: literature; literary art as a field
note: Mandarin means one concrete text; Vietnamese means the whole art form. A Mandarin 文章 is a Vietnamese bài viết.

mandarinMeaning: a surgical operation; surgery
vietnameseMeaning: a technique, trick or manoeuvre (often a sly one)
note: Vietnamese does keep a minor medical 'minor procedure' sense, but the everyday meaning is a trick or knack. Vietnamese for surgery is phẫu thuật.

mandarinMeaning: an accident (typically causing injury or damage)
vietnameseMeaning: an incident, fault, malfunction or outage
note: Vietnamese sự cố is often a technical glitch with nobody hurt. Mandarin 交通事故 is a traffic accident; Vietnamese would use tai nạn for that.

mandarinMeaning: a disaster; a catastrophe (large-scale)
vietnameseMeaning: an accident (e.g. a traffic accident), usually individual-scale
note: A scale mismatch. Mandarin 灾难 is an earthquake or a famine; Vietnamese tai nạn is typically one crash. Mandarin for that is 事故.

mandarinMeaning: crystal; rock crystal
vietnameseMeaning: glass (the everyday material)
note: Vietnamese ly thủy tinh is an ordinary glass tumbler, not crystal. Mandarin for glass is 玻璃 bōli.

mandarinMeaning: land; soil; territory
vietnameseMeaning: the local earth god of folk religion
note: Mandarin also has the deity sense (土地公), but its ordinary meaning is plain land. Vietnamese for land is đất or đất đai.

mandarinMeaning: famous; well-known (positive)
vietnameseMeaning: nominal; in name only (usually negative)
note: Vietnamese hữu danh mostly survives in hữu danh vô thực 'famous in name but empty in substance'. For 'famous' Vietnamese says nổi tiếng.

mandarinMeaning: self-respect; to take care of one's own good name
vietnameseMeaning: to be thin-skinned; easily offended; touchy pride
note: Mandarin is a virtue, Vietnamese is a flaw. Telling someone they have tự ái is a criticism.

mandarinMeaning: to operate; to run (of a machine); to revolve
vietnameseMeaning: to transport; to move goods from place to place
note: Mandarin describes a machine turning over; Vietnamese describes freight moving. Mandarin for transport is 运输 yùnshū.

mandarinMeaning: to install; a device, unit or installation
vietnameseMeaning: to decorate; decoration
note: Installing equipment versus hanging decorations. Vietnamese for the Mandarin sense is lắp đặt or thiết bị.

mandarinMeaning: rules; regulations; articles of association; a charter
vietnameseMeaning: a programme; a schedule; a TV show; a curriculum
note: High-frequency in Vietnamese with the 'programme' sense (chương trình TV). Mandarin 章程 is a legal/constitutional document; its word for programme is 节目 or 程序.

mandarinMeaning: a straight line (geometry); sharply (of a rise or fall)
vietnameseMeaning: online (on the internet)
note: Vietnamese học trực tuyến is 'study online'. Mandarin uses 在线 zàixiàn for that; 直线 is strictly geometric.

mandarinMeaning: repeatedly; over and over; to vacillate
vietnameseMeaning: treacherous; disloyal; to betray
note: Mandarin 反复练习 means 'practise repeatedly', with no disloyalty implied. Vietnamese phản phúc accuses someone of betrayal.

mandarinMeaning: raw material; ingredients; (also) data or material for a report
vietnameseMeaning: documents; files; reference material
note: The senses overlap on 'material for a report', but Mandarin's primary meaning is physical stuff (建筑材料 'building materials'). Vietnamese for that is vật liệu.

mandarinMeaning: the environment (natural or physical surroundings)
vietnameseMeaning: circumstances; a person's situation in life
note: Mandarin 保护环境 is 'protect the environment'. Vietnamese hoàn cảnh is usually someone's personal circumstances (hoàn cảnh khó khăn). Vietnamese for the ecological sense is môi trường.

mandarinMeaning: interest paid on a loan or deposit
vietnameseMeaning: income, profit or yield more broadly
note: Mandarin is specifically bank interest; Vietnamese lợi tức is a wider earnings notion. Vietnamese for bank interest is lãi suất or tiền lãi.

mandarinMeaning: a secretary; an administrative assistant
vietnameseMeaning: a Party Secretary (a senior political office)
note: A large status inversion. Vietnamese bí thư tỉnh ủy is a provincial party chief. For an office secretary Vietnamese says thư ký.

mandarinMeaning: a Party Secretary (senior political post); also a clerk
vietnameseMeaning: an office secretary; a clerk; a minute-taker
note: The exact mirror image of 秘书/bí thư — the two languages swapped which word carries political rank. Worth learning as a pair.

mandarinMeaning: happy; joyful (the ordinary word, as in 生日快乐)
vietnameseMeaning: hedonistic pleasure, often carnal or indulgent
note: 生日快乐 'happy birthday' is everyday Mandarin. Vietnamese khoái lạc carries a sensual, indulgent charge; the neutral word is vui or hạnh phúc.

mandarinMeaning: cheap; inexpensive
vietnameseMeaning: amenities; comfortable, well-appointed
note: Price versus comfort. A Vietnamese phòng tiện nghi is a well-equipped room, which may be anything but 便宜.

mandarinMeaning: lively; bustling; buzzing with activity (positive in Mandarin)
vietnameseMeaning: noisy, boisterous, rowdy (often mildly negative)
note: Mandarin 很热闹 is a compliment about atmosphere. The Vietnamese cognate leans towards unwanted noise. Note the Vietnamese word also reverses the character order.

mandarinMeaning: winding, tortuous; (of a story) complicated with twists
vietnameseMeaning: concise, clear and well-articulated
note: Nearly opposite in evaluation: Mandarin implies convoluted, Vietnamese implies lucid.

mandarinMeaning: vigorous; flourishing; thriving (positive)
vietnameseMeaning: impetuous; immature; rashly impulsive (negative)
note: Mandarin 蓬勃发展 is 'booming development'. Vietnamese bồng bột describes a young person acting without thinking.

mandarinMeaning: tall and sturdily built; burly
vietnameseMeaning: handsome, of fine appearance (especially of a young man)
note: Mandarin is about physical bulk, Vietnamese about good looks.

mandarinMeaning: human feeling; social obligation; a favour owed
vietnameseMeaning: a lover; a mistress
note: Mandarin 人情 is the currency of reciprocal favours. Vietnamese nhân tình is a romantic partner outside marriage.

mandarinMeaning: a successful candidate in the highest imperial examination (historical only)
vietnameseMeaning: a PhD; a doctoral degree holder (current, everyday)
note: Mandarin 进士 is purely historical; nobody is one today. Vietnamese tiến sĩ is the live modern word for a doctorate — which Mandarin expresses as 博士.

mandarinMeaning: a successful candidate in the provincial imperial examination (historical)
vietnameseMeaning: a bachelor's degree holder (current, everyday)
note: Same historical-versus-modern split as 进士/tiến sĩ. Vietnamese repurposed the old examination ranks for modern degrees; Mandarin did not.

mandarinMeaning: a licentiate preparing for imperial examinations (archaic)
vietnameseMeaning: a university student (current, extremely common)
note: Vietnamese sinh viên is the everyday word for an undergraduate. Mandarin 生员 is archaic; the modern word is 大学生.

mandarinMeaning: buried treasure; precious mineral deposits
vietnameseMeaning: a museum
note: Vietnamese viện bảo tàng is a museum building. Mandarin 宝藏 is the treasure itself; a museum is 博物馆 bówùguǎn.

mandarinMeaning: a country's territory or domain
vietnameseMeaning: a map (the printed or drawn object)
note: Vietnamese bản đồ is the piece of paper. Mandarin 版图 is the land itself; a map is 地图 dìtú.

mandarinMeaning: a sign, mark, symbol or logo; to indicate
vietnameseMeaning: a criterion; a standard for judging
note: Mandarin 标志 is something you look at; Vietnamese tiêu chí is something you measure against. Vietnamese for a sign is biển báo or ký hiệu.

mandarinMeaning: to ravage; to devastate; to wreck (a transitive verb)
vietnameseMeaning: shabby, dilapidated, in a sorry state (an adjective)
note: Mandarin names the destructive act, Vietnamese the resulting shabby condition.

mandarinMeaning: to dispatch or assign (especially troops or personnel)
vietnameseMeaning: to control or operate (a machine, a vehicle, a remote)
note: Vietnamese điều khiển từ xa is a remote control. Mandarin 调遣 is about sending people somewhere.

mandarinMeaning: to produce a sound; to vocalize; to voice a view
vietnameseMeaning: radio broadcasting
note: Vietnamese đài phát thanh is a radio station. Mandarin 发声 is any act of making sound; broadcasting is 广播.

mandarinMeaning: father and elder brothers; the head of a family
vietnameseMeaning: a parent or guardian (as in school communications)
note: Vietnamese họp phụ huynh is a parents' meeting at school. Mandarin 父兄 is literal male kin and is not the word used for parents (that is 家长).

mandarinMeaning: level; flat; smooth (of ground or a road)
vietnameseMeaning: calm; composed; unruffled (of a person's demeanour)
note: Mandarin describes terrain, Vietnamese describes temperament.

mandarinMeaning: to drift on a current; to float; river rafting
vietnameseMeaning: adventure; to adventure
note: Mandarin is passive drifting; Vietnamese phiêu lưu is deliberate adventure (truyện phiêu lưu 'adventure story').

mandarinMeaning: very; extremely; utterly (a common intensifier)
vietnameseMeaning: decimal (the base-10 number system)
note: Mandarin 十分好 is 'very good'. Vietnamese thập phân is a mathematics term — số thập phân 'decimal number'.

mandarinMeaning: current affairs; the present state of things
vietnameseMeaning: the TV news programme
note: Vietnamese xem thời sự means watching the evening news broadcast. Mandarin 时事 is the subject matter, not the programme.

mandarinMeaning: the Milky Way specifically (poetic)
vietnameseMeaning: a galaxy (any galaxy, the general astronomical term)
note: Vietnamese thiên hà is the generic scientific word. Mandarin's generic term is 星系; 天河 names our own galaxy poetically.

mandarinMeaning: gymnastics (one specific sport)
vietnameseMeaning: sport in general; athletics as a whole
note: A narrow-to-broad jump. Vietnamese thể thao covers all sport; Mandarin's equivalent is 体育. 体操 is only gymnastics.

mandarinMeaning: to update; to renew; to upgrade (software, records)
vietnameseMeaning: to reform or modernize (historical, of a nation)
note: Mandarin 更新 is what your phone does. Vietnamese canh tân evokes 19th-century national reform movements; for software Vietnamese says cập nhật.

mandarinMeaning: a contingency plan (for emergencies)
vietnameseMeaning: a project (business, construction, development)
note: Vietnamese dự án đầu tư is an investment project. Mandarin's word for that is 项目; 预案 is specifically an emergency plan.

mandarinMeaning: a way of doing something; a means; a solution (everyday, neutral)
vietnameseMeaning: a measure, especially an official or remedial one
note: Mild. Mandarin 没办法 'there's no way' is casual everyday speech; Vietnamese biện pháp is more formal and policy-flavoured (biện pháp phòng chống). Vietnamese casual equivalent is cách.

mandarinMeaning: service; to serve (commercial, e.g. customer service)
vietnameseMeaning: to serve, especially in an official or waiting-on capacity
note: Mild. Mandarin 服务 works as a noun for the commercial abstraction (服务业 'service industry'); Vietnamese phục vụ is chiefly the verb, with dịch vụ used for the noun.
